summary: self-certificates ships fake PEM that fetches and executes remote Python payload
details: The package ships test/key.pem framed as an RSA private key, but its body is a two-layer base64 blob that decodes to a JavaScript IIFE which fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes the response body into python3 via child_process.spawn with detached and windowsHide flags. index.js reads test/key.pem, strips the PEM headers, base64-decodes the body, and passes the decoded payload as a third argument to selfsign.generate, making the fetch-and-exec chain reachable through require('self-certificates'). The URL itself is stored as a second-layer base64 literal (aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHR1cGRhdGUub3JnL3NldHRpbmdzL3ByaXZhY3kucGhw) to hide the destination, and the PEM cover-story exists to disguise executable JavaScript as inert key material.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
